perspective:
Christian has access to the following information:

- He is a police officer. Jonathan is his childhood friend/best friend; Christian trusts him, often seeks his advice, and values his perspective.
- Christian felt Jonathan was hiding something important, which made him anxious and suspicious. He arranged a meeting at their favorite coffee shop and confronted Jonathan.
- Jonathan told him: he could trust Jonathan; Jonathan had been hiding something; Jonathan is in some trouble and didn’t know how to tell him.
- Christian offered help. Jonathan said the situation is complicated, he didn’t want to drag Christian in, but he could use support and resources to get out of the mess.
- Christian asked if the trouble was illegal. Jonathan said he couldn’t say for sure, might have gotten involved with the wrong people, but claimed he didn’t do anything illegal himself.
- Christian decided to investigate discreetly to ensure Jonathan’s safety without alarming him. Jonathan thanked him and trusted him to handle it carefully.
- Christian’s investigation led him to believe Jonathan was being framed. He told Jonathan this, said he had leads but didn’t yet know who was responsible, and planned to gather more evidence to prove Jonathan’s innocence. Jonathan thanked him.
- Later, Christian concluded he had found out who was behind it: someone close to both of them whom they both knew and trusted. He felt betrayed and resolute, and planned to confront that person and bring them to justice. Jonathan warned him the person was dangerous but said he trusted Christian to do what was right.
- Christian believes he knows the culprit’s identity, but the specific name is not given in the provided dialogue.
